title: Enforcement Decree of the Act on Protection of Specific Crime Informants, etc.
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on Protection of Specific Crime Informants, etc. and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Qualifications of Assistants to Crime Informants, Etc.) "Persons prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 6 (2) of the Act on Protection of Specific Crime Informants, etc. (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means persons falling under any of the following subparagraphs:
1. The heads or employees of schools, social education facilities, social welfare facilities, and social protection facilities;
2. The heads or employees of counseling centers prescribed by statutes, such as the Legal Aid Act;
3. Employers of crime informants, etc.;
4. Other persons of learning and virtue who are recognized as capable of providing sufficient assistance to crime informants, etc.

Article 3 (Payment of Actual Expenses to Assistants, Etc.)
(1) Expenses that may be paid to assistants to crime informants, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "assistants") pursuant to Article 6 (10) of the Act shall be daily allowances, travel expenses, and lodging expenses according to the number of days on which they accompany crime informants, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "actual expenses" in this Article).
(2) Actual expenses under paragraph (1) shall be paid in the same manner as for a person making a statement or a witness according to the stage of the relevant case, and shall be paid by the investigative agency at the investigation stage and by the court at the trial stage, respectively.

Article 4 (Matters to Be Entered in Identity Management Cards)
(1) The identity management card for crime informants, etc. under Article 7 (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "identity management card") shall state matters by which the identity of crime informants, etc. can be ascertained, such as their names, resident registration numbers, addresses, and occupations, and matters concerning assistants, defense counsel, personal safety measures under Article 13 of the Act, payment of relief funds under Article 14 of the Act, etc.
(2) Where crime informants, etc. sign records, etc. using an assumed name pursuant to Article 7 (4) of the Act, the prosecutor or judicial police officer shall enter the assumed name stated in the record in the identity management card and shall have the crime informants, etc. sign both their real names and assumed names on the identity management card and affix their thumbprints thereto.

Article 5 (Management of Identity Management Cards)
(1) When a judicial police officer forwards a case, the officer shall seal the identity management card separately from the investigation documents and submit it to the competent prosecutors' office together with the case records.
(2) The head of each prosecutors' office (including the head of a branch office of a district prosecutors' office) shall designate a prosecutor to manage identity management cards.
(3) The prosecutor under paragraph (2) shall manage identity management cards even after a public prosecution has been instituted.
(4) When the identity of a witness is verified pursuant to the latter part of Article 11 (3) of the Act, the prosecutor shall present the identity management card directly to the presiding judge or judge in the courtroom, and the presiding judge or judge shall, without delay, have the court administrative official, etc. in charge verify the identity using the identity management card.

Article 6 (Requests for Personal Safety Measures, Etc.)
(1) A request or application for personal safety measures under Article 13 (1) through (3) of the Act shall be made in writing (including an electronic document; hereinafter the same shall apply): Provided, That in an urgent case, it may be made orally or by telephone, but the relevant written document shall be submitted afterwards without delay. <Amended on March 17, 2004>
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the presiding judge or judge may orally request a prosecutor appearing in the courtroom to take personal safety measures. In such cases, the purport thereof shall be entered in the trial record.
(3) When intending to request or apply for personal safety measures pursuant to paragraph (1), the types and duration of the necessary personal safety measures shall be specifically stated.
(4) Where the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency (including the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard; hereinafter the same shall apply) or the commissioner of a City/Do police agency (including the commissioner of a regional coast guard agency; hereinafter the same shall apply) needs to take personal safety measures for crime informants, etc. or their relatives, etc. in a case under investigation by the relevant agency, the Commissioner General or commissioner may direct the chief of the police station (including the chief of a coast guard station; hereinafter the same shall apply) having jurisdiction over the residence or current location of the person concerned to take personal safety measures. <Amended on November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017; December 31, 2020>

Article 7 (Types of Personal Safety Measures)
The types of personal safety measures under Article 13 (1) of the Act shall be any of the following:
1. Protection in a specified facility for a specified period;
2. Personal guarding for a specified period;
3. Accompanying a person when appearing as a person giving a statement or a witness and when returning home;
4. Regular patrols of the residence of the person concerned;
5. Other measures deemed necessary for personal safety.

Article 8 (Notification of Implementation of Personal Safety Measures, etc.)
(1) Where the chief of a police station takes personal safety measures under Article 13 (1) of the Act, the chief shall notify the relevant prosecutor specified in the following subparagraphs of that fact without delay: <Amended on December 31, 2020>
1. Where the personal safety measures are taken at the request of a prosecutor: The prosecutor who made the request;
2. Where the personal safety measures are taken upon instructions from the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency or the commissioner of a City/Do police agency, or at the request of the chief of a police station: A prosecutor of the district prosecutors' office or branch office having jurisdiction over the police agency to which the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency or commissioner of a City/Do police agency who first issued the instructions, or the chief of a police station who first made the request, belongs;
3. Where the personal safety measures are taken upon the application of crime informants, etc., their legal representatives, or their relatives, etc.: The prosecutor handling the case, or a prosecutor of the district prosecutors' office or branch office having jurisdiction over the police agency handling the case.
(2) Notification documents under paragraph (1) and documents related to personal safety measures shall not be disclosed.

Article 9 (Calculation of Relief Funds)
(1) Relief funds under Article 14 of the Act shall be calculated to include medical expenses, living expenses, moving and job change expenses, installation costs for security facilities, expenses necessary for the protection or guarding of crime informants, etc. or their relatives, etc. during the investigation, and compensation for emotional distress, etc., that have been incurred or need to be incurred.
(2) Of the relief funds under paragraph (1), medical expenses, moving expenses, installation costs for security facilities, and expenses necessary for the protection or guarding of crime informants, etc. or their relatives, etc. shall be paid at actual cost.
(3) Of the relief funds under paragraph (1), living expenses, job change expenses, and compensation for emotional distress may be combined and paid as a fixed monthly amount. In such cases, the amount shall be calculated, according to the occupational category of the recipient of the relief funds, on the basis of an amount not exceeding five times the daily minimum wage prescribed by the Minimum Wage Act at the time of the decision on relief.

Article 10 (Applications for Relief Funds)
Where crime informants, etc., their legal representatives, or their relatives, etc. intend to receive relief funds under Article 14 of the Act, they shall apply to the Crime Informant Relief Deliberative Council of the district prosecutors' office having jurisdiction over the area where the crime reporting, etc. under subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Act took place (hereinafter referred to as the “Council”). In such cases, crime informants, etc. whose names were not entered in records, etc. pursuant to Article 7 (4) of the Act may apply under a pseudonym.

Article 11 (Decisions on Relief)
(1) Where an application for relief funds is made under Article 10, the Council shall, unless there are special reasons, decide whether to pay relief funds within one month from the date of application (including the amount where it decides to make payment; hereinafter the same shall apply).
(2) Where urgent reasons preclude following the procedures under Article 10 or paragraph (1), a prosecutor may request the Council to make a provisional payment of costs and other amounts necessary for protecting or guarding crime informants, etc. or their relatives, etc., or for similar purposes. In such cases, notwithstanding paragraph (1), the Council may decide to make a provisional payment.

Article 12 (Jurisdiction of the Council)
The territorial jurisdiction of the Council shall be the territorial jurisdiction of the district prosecutors' office in which the Council is established (including the territorial jurisdiction of any branch office).

Article 13 (Composition of the Council)
The Council shall consist of the deputy chief prosecutor of the district prosecutors' office in which the Council is established, serving as chairperson, and four members appointed or commissioned by the Minister of Justice from among public officials of that district prosecutors' office and persons qualified to serve as judges.

Article 14 (Chairperson)
(1) The chairperson of the Council shall direct the affairs of the Council and represent the Council.
(2) Where the chairperson is unable to perform the duties of office for an unavoidable reason, a member designated in advance by the chairperson shall act on the chairperson's behalf; where no such designation has been made, the senior member among those who are public officials of the institution in which the Council is established shall act on the chairperson's behalf.

Article 15 (Proceedings of the Council)
(1) The chairperson shall convene meetings of the Council (hereinafter referred to as "meetings") and preside over them.
(2) A meeting shall be convened with the attendance of a majority of all incumbent members, including the chairperson, and resolutions shall be adopted with the affirmative votes of at least two-thirds of the members present.
(3) Where opinions on the amount of relief funds are divided into three or more amounts and none reaches the two-thirds voting quorum, the votes for larger amounts shall successively be added to the votes for the smallest amount until the two-thirds voting quorum is reached, and the highest amount among those thus included shall be adopted.

Article 16 (Administrative Staff)
(1) The Council shall have one executive secretary and several clerks to handle its affairs.
(2) The executive secretary and clerks shall be appointed by the chief prosecutor of the district prosecutors' office in which the Council is established, upon the recommendation of the chairperson, from among public officials belonging to that district prosecutors' office.
(3) The executive secretary shall handle the affairs of the Council under the orders of the chairperson.
(4) The executive secretary may attend and speak at meetings.
(5) The clerks shall assist the executive secretary and manage documents related to the Council.

Article 17 (Direction and Supervision by the Minister of Justice)
(1) The Minister of Justice may issue orders or take measures necessary to direct and supervise each Council.
(2) Where the Minister of Justice deems it necessary for performing the duties under paragraph (1), the Minister may have staff members under the Minister's jurisdiction or prosecutors of prosecutors' offices at each level audit the handling of affairs by each Council.

Article 18 (Decision and Notification)
(1) Where the Council makes a decision on relief, it shall prepare a written decision on relief, and all members who attended the meeting shall sign or affix their seals thereto.
(2) A written decision on relief under paragraph (1) shall state the following matters:
1. The applicant's name, address, and resident registration number (only the pseudonym shall be stated in cases falling under Article 7 (4) of the Act);
2. The operative provisions of the decision;
3. The reasons;
4. The date of the decision.
(3) Where the Council makes a decision on relief, it shall send a notice of the decision on relief to the applicant.

Article 19 (Claims for Payment of Relief Funds)
(1) A person who intends to claim payment of relief funds shall submit a written claim for payment of relief funds to the district prosecutors' office in which the Council that made the decision on relief is established.
(2) A written claim under paragraph (1) shall state the following matters:
1. The claimant's name, address, and resident registration number (only the pseudonym shall be stated in cases falling under Article 7 (4) of the Act);
2. The number of the decision on relief and the operative provisions of the decision;
3. The date of the claim.

Article 20 (Forms, etc.)
Matters concerning forms, etc. necessary for the enforcement of the Act and this Decree shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Justice.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 16815, May 25, 2000>

This Decree shall enter into force on June 1, 2000.

ADDENDA (Decree Amending the Regulations on Management of Parolees and Other Regulations for Electronic Processing of Civil Petitions) <Presidential Decree No. 18312, March 17, 2004>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA (Organization of the Ministry of the Interior and Its Affiliated Agencies) <Presidential Decree No. 25751, November 19, 2014>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation: Provided, That among the Presidential Decrees amended pursuant to Article 5 of the Addenda, the portions amending Presidential Decrees that were promulgated before this Decree enters into force but whose enforcement dates have not yet arrived shall enter into force on the respective enforcement dates of those Presidential Decrees.

Articles 2 through 4 Omitted.

Article 5 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) through (81) Omitted.
(82) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on Protection of Specific Crime Informants, etc. is partially amended as follows:
In Article 6 (4), "Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard" shall be replaced by "Minister of Public Safety and Security", "commissioner of a regional police agency" shall be replaced by "commissioner of a regional police agency (including the head of a regional maritime security and safety headquarters; hereinafter the same shall apply)", and "chief of a coast guard station" shall be replaced by "chief of a maritime security and safety station".
(83) through (418) Omitted.

ADDENDA (Organization of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and Its Affiliated Agencies) <Presidential Decree No. 28211, July 26, 2017>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation: Provided, That among the Presidential Decrees amended pursuant to Article 8 of the Addenda, the portions amending Presidential Decrees that were promulgated before this Decree enters into force but whose enforcement dates have not yet arrived shall enter into force on the respective enforcement dates of those Presidential Decrees.

Articles 2 through 7 Omitted.

Article 8 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) through (74) Omitted.
(75) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on Protection of Specific Crime Informants, etc. is partially amended as follows:
In Article 6 (4), "Minister of Public Safety and Security" shall be replaced by "Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard", "head of a regional maritime security and safety headquarters" shall be replaced by "commissioner of a regional coast guard agency", and "chief of a maritime security and safety station" shall be replaced by "chief of a coast guard station".
(76) through (388) Omitted.

ADDENDA (Regulations on Autonomous Police Affairs and the Organization and Operation of City/Do Autonomous Police Committees, etc.) <Presidential Decree No. 31349, December 31, 2020>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on January 1, 2021.

Articles 2 and 3 Omitted.

Article 4 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) through (45) Omitted.
(46) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on Protection of Specific Crime Informants, etc. is partially amended as follows:
In Articles 6 (4) and 8 (1) 2, "commissioner of a regional police agency" shall be replaced by "commissioner of a City/Do police agency", respectively.
(47) through (49) Omitted.
